'''Robert J. Seiwald''' (born March 26, 1925) is an American retired [[chemist]]. He was born in [[Fort Morgan, Colorado|Fort Morgan]], [[Morgan County, Colorado]]. An only child, his parents were farmers. His father died in 1934 of [[pneumonia]], while his mother died of [[breast cancer]] in 1935. Prior to enlisting in the [[United States Army]] during [[World War II]] in 1944, he enrolled at the [[University of San Francisco]], where he majored in chemistry. During the war, he was a [[rifleman]] in the [[89th Infantry Division (United States)|89th Infantry Division]] and went to Europe on a ship. In 1954, he studied for his [[Doctor of philosophy|Ph.D.]] at [[Saint Louis University (United States)|St. Louis University]].<ref name="GPark23">{{cite web|url=https://www.glenparkassociation.org/from-a-destitute-okie-to-a-really-good-life-in-glen-park-bob-seiwald-of-burnside-avenue/|title=From a destitute Okie to a "really good life" in Glen Park: Bob Seiwald of Burnside Avenue|publisher=Glen Park Association|date=June 9, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2024}}</ref>

In 1960, Seiwald and [[Joseph H. Burckhalter]] received a [[patent]] while working at [[University of Kansas]], for their work on fluorescein [[fluorescein isothiocyanate]] and [[Rhodamine|rhodamine isothiocyanate]], the former being an [[antibody]] labeling agent which helps accurately diagnosing various diseases. In 1957, he returned to the University of San Francisco as an organic chemistry professor, a position he held until his retirement in 1999. In 1995, Seiwald and Burckhalter were inducted into the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]].<ref name="NHF">{{cite web|url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/robert-j-seiwald|title= Robert J. Seiwald - Isothiocyanate Compounds for Antigen Identification|publisher=[[National Inventors Hall of Fame]]|access-date=October 18, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Seiwald married Joan Walter in 1956. They were married until her death in on May 11, 2023, at the age of 91. The couple had five children in total.<ref name="GParkObit">{{cite web|url=https://www.glenparkassociation.org/glen-park-icon-joan-seiwald-long-time-sfusd-staffer-park-saver-and-as-fan/|title=Glen Park icon Joan Seiwald: Long-time SFUSD staffer, park-saver and A's fan|publisher=Glen Park Association|date=May 22, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2024}}</ref>
